title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning Procedures in Cases of Personal Safety Protection Orders

articles.content_en: I. The issue of whether litigation fees shall be charged in personal safety protection order cases. This court agrees with your court's prevailing opinion that no litigation fees shall be charged for applying to the People's Court for a personal safety protection order.

II. The issue of whether security needs to be provided when applying for a personal safety protection order. This court agrees with your court's prevailing opinion that, when requesting the People's Court to issue a personal safety protection order in accordance with the Anti-Domestic Violence Law of the People's Republic of China, the applicant shall not need to provide security.

III. Issues concerning the applicable procedure for personal safety protection order cases, etc. The Anti-Domestic Violence Law does not directly stipulate which procedure shall apply to personal safety protection order cases. The People's Court may hear such cases by analogy with special procedures. Where a party in a family dispute case applies to the People's Court for a personal safety protection order, the adjudication organization hearing the case shall render a ruling on whether to issue the personal safety protection order; if the applicant for the personal safety protection order has no ongoing family case proceedings before the People's Court accepting the application, the judge shall hear the case sitting alone. As to whether it is necessary to hear the respondent's opinions on the issuance of the personal safety protection order, the presiding judge shall decide it based on the specific circumstances of the case.

IV. The issue of reconsideration. A reconsideration application filed by the respondent against a personal safety protection order and a reconsideration application filed by the applicant against a dismissal ruling may be reviewed by the original adjudication organization; if the People's Court deems it necessary, it may also designate another adjudication organization to conduct the reconsideration.
This is hereby replied.
